The reverse operation represents a specific task. Placing it in a separate method allows the same logic to be reused by other number manipulation programs.
10. How can you find the sum of the digits of a number?

14. What is the purpose of a method in number manipulation programs?
A method is used to perform a particular task.
Separate methods make the logic reusable and keep the main program smaller.
15. Why should the main method contain mainly method calls?
The number-processing logic can be placed inside separate methods. The main method can then collect input, call the required methods, and process their returned values.
This keeps the main method simple and avoids putting a large amount of logic into one place.
16. How can a power operation be reused in number manipulation programs?
A power method can accept a base and an exponent and return the calculated value.
For example, while checking an Armstrong number, the extracted digit can be passed as the base and the digit count as the exponent.
17. What is an Armstrong number according to the program logic?
For an Armstrong number, each digit is raised to the power of the number of digits, and all the resulting values are added.
If the final sum is equal to the original number, the number is considered an Armstrong number.
